title: Symptoms You Can't Describe? Show Them to AI: Ant Afu Upgrades Real-Time Video Consultation

content_html:
Something feels wrong with your body, but you can’t quite say where the problem is—this “can’t put it into words” frustration is quite common. On November 23, at the Ant A Fu Healthcare Ecosystem Conference, the A Fu App announced a major upgrade. Built on the Bailing medical and healthcare model series, it focuses on two things: real-time video “look, listen, ask, and check” consultations, and centralized management of the whole family’s health records.

The camera is the stethoscope

Open the real-time audio/video feature in the lower right corner of the A Fu homepage, and health checks shift from typing to face-to-face conversation. For skin changes or areas of discomfort, just point the camera at them and show A Fu; medicine boxes and physical exam reports at home can also be held up to the camera for recognition. Sound is a clue too—different coughs, snores, and wheezing sounds are captured in real time, and A Fu then proactively asks follow-up questions based on how long they last and the situations in which they occur.

Shoulder discomfort? Follow the prompts to raise and lower your arm; the range of motion and location of pain are both included in the analysis. If you wear a continuous glucose monitor or smartwatch, blood sugar fluctuations and heart rate changes are also factored in. When in doubt, you can switch to a real doctor for face-to-face communication with one tap during the video call.

One person’s consultation, the whole family’s records

Another upgrade targets families: scattered health information is gathered into “Health Items,” and the whole family’s updates can be seen on one page—your own weight-loss progress, your baby’s feeding and vaccine schedule, and your parents’ blood sugar records—no more digging through separate accounts. Around the three most common needs—weight loss, blood sugar control, and parenting—A Fu also provides dedicated assistants that offer personalized plans based on diet, exercise, blood sugar, or growth records.

A further change lies in being “proactive”: if you go to bed too late for several days in a row, or your parents’ blood sugar fluctuates abnormally, A Fu will proactively remind you; health goals set during conversations are automatically turned into daily action items, and a weekly report is generated on weekends to review how well they were carried out.
